BiblicalUsage: Gannab is the thief, the stealer, and the prophets use him as the picture of a guilty nation. If a man is found stealing a brother, the thief shall die, says Deuteronomy 24:7. The thief comes in by night in Hosea 7:1, the princes are companions of thieves in Isaiah 1:23, and the house of Israel is ashamed as the thief is ashamed when he is found in Jeremiah 2:26.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the thief is ashamed when he is found, and so are we. The law, the prophets, and the shame all point the same way: what is taken in secret will be found out. I hold that the only thief who goes free is the one who confesses and restores.
